title: Stone Age to Iron Age
intro: Hunter-gatherers, stone circles, bronze tools and hillforts in prehistoric Britain.

questions.prompt: Which famous prehistoric stone circle stands in Wiltshire?
questions.explanation: Stonehenge is a huge prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire.

questions.prompt: Which of these periods came first?
questions.explanation: The Stone Age came first, then the Bronze Age, then the Iron Age, before the Romans arrived.

questions.prompt: Bronze is made by mixing copper with which other metal?
questions.explanation: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. It is harder than copper alone, so it made better tools.

questions.prompt: How did people in the early Stone Age mainly get their food?
questions.explanation: Early Stone Age people were hunter-gatherers who hunted animals and gathered wild plants, nuts and berries.

questions.prompt: Skara Brae is a Stone Age village found in which part of the UK?
questions.explanation: Skara Brae, in Orkney, is a very well-preserved Stone Age village with stone furniture still inside the houses.

questions.prompt: Many Iron Age people in Britain lived in roundhouses.
questions.explanation: Roundhouses had circular walls and cone-shaped thatched roofs, with a fire in the middle.

questions.prompt: In which period were many hillforts built in Britain?
questions.explanation: Hillforts, protected by banks and ditches, were especially common during the Iron Age.

questions.prompt: What did Stone Age people often use flint for?
questions.explanation: Flint can be chipped to give a sharp edge, so it was used for axes, knives, scrapers and arrowheads.

questions.prompt: Stone Age people lived at the same time as the dinosaurs.
questions.explanation: The dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, long before the first people lived.
